messages.content: Let's turn the Upper Midwest holds into actual reservations tonight. Use the Sunday afternoon to Chicago and Friday out of Milwaukee plan unless something has gotten worse. The only thing I still need to decide is Thursday night: stay west-side Milwaukee or move by the airport.

I would keep Thursday west-side. With the current Friday departure at 12:12 p.m., the airport move only saves about 20 to 25 minutes, and it adds a second hotel check-in after the Wauwatosa day. If you leave the west-side hotel around 8:45, fuel by 9:10, and return the car at MKE by 10:00 to 10:15, the buffer is still comfortable.
Okay, keep both Milwaukee nights west-side. Please make the Friday buffer visible in the notes so I don't accidentally treat it like a leisurely morning.

Done. Flight pair to book: Delta SLC to ORD on Sunday Oct 27, 2:20 p.m. to 6:06 p.m., nonstop. Return: Delta MKE to SLC on Friday Nov 1, 12:12 p.m. to 4:03 p.m. via MSP, with a 71-minute connection. I requested window seats where available and noted that the return connection should not be tightened.
Good. And the car is still Chicago pickup, Milwaukee return?

Yes. Rental is set for ORD pickup Sunday at 6:45 p.m. and MKE return Friday at 10:15 a.m. The one-way fee is shown on the estimate, so finance can see why the open-jaw plan costs more than a Chicago round trip. Add fuel stop Friday before the airport and save the final rental receipt, fuel receipt, parking receipts, and hotel folios.
Walk me through the hotels before you book them. I want to be sure the breakfast and parking details are not buried.

Hotel set: Oak Brook area Sunday and Monday at Hyatt House Oak Brook, queen room, breakfast 6:30 to 9:30, self-parking included, cancel by 6 p.m. Oct 25. Madison Tuesday at Hampton near campus, queen room, breakfast starts 6:00, parking about $18 to $22, cancel by 6 p.m. Oct 27. Milwaukee Wednesday and Thursday at Residence Inn Milwaukee West, queen studio, breakfast 6:30 to 9:30, parking included, cancel by 6 p.m. Oct 28.
Madison is the one I worry about. If that breakfast changes earlier, will the hotel breakfast still work?

For the current 7:20 a.m. check-in, yes, as long as you keep it to grab-and-go. If the host moves it earlier than about 7:10, plan on taking coffee, yogurt, or a bar from the lobby and not relying on a plated breakfast. I added that as a note rather than assuming the full breakfast will be usable.

messages.content: The Wisconsin loop is finally done, and now I have a mid-November Idaho add-on. Monday afternoon travel, Tuesday 7:30 counselor breakfast in Boise, Tuesday evening fair in Nampa, Wednesday morning high-school visit in Twin Falls, then home to Salt Lake Wednesday night. Can you compare driving with flying into Boise and renting a car?

Yes. Short version: drive if the I-84 forecast is clean; fly-and-rent only helps if Monday weather between Salt Lake and Boise looks messy. You still have to handle the Boise/Nampa to Twin Falls stretch either way, so flying does not remove the winter-road issue entirely.
Give me the trade-offs plainly.

Drive: leave Salt Lake around 1:00 p.m. Monday, reach Boise about 6:30 to 7:00 with one stop, no airport or rental delay, lowest cost, flexible Wednesday return. Risk is weather and fatigue on I-84. Fly and rent: take a Monday afternoon SLC-BOI nonstop, rent at Boise, then either one-way the car toward Twin Falls or backtrack to Boise. It is easier Monday but more expensive and less flexible, especially if the Twin Falls flight timing or one-way rental is poor.
What would you actually recommend?

For now, hold refundable hotels and plan to drive. Put a weather decision point on Sunday evening and again Monday by 9:00 a.m. If snow, wind, or chain controls are likely on I-84, pivot to the afternoon Boise flight and a rental. If the roads are just cold and clear, driving is the simpler loop.
Where should I stay Monday and Tuesday?

Monday: stay in Boise near downtown or Boise State if the breakfast is central. That protects the 7:30 start and leaves dinner options nearby. Meridian is fine only if the breakfast is west Boise; it helps Nampa but adds morning risk. Tuesday: move to Twin Falls after the Nampa fair if you can safely drive the two hours that night. That makes Wednesday morning much calmer than leaving Boise before dawn.
I like that, but the Nampa fair may run until 8:30. Is the late drive to Twin Falls still okay?

It is acceptable if the weather is dry and you eat before leaving Nampa. Plan 8:45 departure, arrive Twin Falls around 10:45, and keep check-in notified. If the roads are wet, icy, or visibility is bad, stay Nampa/Meridian Tuesday and leave very early Wednesday, but that is the less comfortable plan.
Shortlist practical hotels with breakfast and dinner access. Nothing resorty.

Boise options: Hampton Inn & Suites Boise-Downtown, breakfast included, restaurants walkable, paid parking; Hyatt Place Boise/Downtown, easy food nearby, breakfast depending on rate; or Homewood Suites Meridian if the breakfast location ends up west, with easier parking but a longer Tuesday morning. Twin Falls options: Fairfield Inn & Suites near Pole Line, Hampton Inn Twin Falls, or TownePlace Suites. All keep you near Blue Lakes/Pole Line restaurants and set up an easy Wednesday school visit.
If I drive, do I need a rental hold at all?

No. If you are approved to use the university vehicle or mileage reimbursement, skip the rental. What I would hold now: refundable Boise room for Monday, refundable Twin Falls room for Tuesday, and a backup refundable Nampa/Meridian room for Tuesday only if weather forces you not to drive after the fair.
And if we pivot to flying?

Backup plan: Monday afternoon SLC to Boise nonstop, rent at BOI, keep the Boise hotel, drive Nampa to Twin Falls Tuesday night if roads allow, and return Wednesday either by a Twin Falls to Salt Lake flight if the timing works or by driving the rental back. Before booking that, check the one-way rental fee and Twin Falls flight availability; those are the two pieces most likely to make the flight plan unattractive.
Go ahead and set the holds and the weather trigger list.

Set holds: Boise downtown/Boise State area Monday, Twin Falls Pole Line/Blue Lakes area Tuesday, plus a cancellable Nampa/Meridian Tuesday backup. Planning assumption is drive: Salt Lake 1:00 p.m. Monday, Boise arrival 6:30 to 7:00, Tuesday breakfast 7:30, Nampa fair, then Twin Falls if roads are dry, return to Salt Lake Wednesday after the school visit. Weather triggers for pivot: snow or freezing rain on I-84, strong crosswinds, closures near the Idaho border, or a forecast that makes the Tuesday night Nampa-to-Twin Falls drive unsafe.
